Taiga is seeking a Manufacturing Engineering Manager to lead our Manufacturing Engineering and Automation team and own the strategy, performance, and continuous improvement of the manufacturing processes behind our electric powersport vehicles and powertrains. This role reports to the VP of Operations and works from the Taiga head office and manufacturing facility in LaSalle, Quebec. 
 Position Summary 
 The Manufacturing Engineering Manager drives production efficiency, throughput, build time optimization, automation initiatives, and tooling investments while serving as the technical leader on the manufacturing floor. Balancing strategic planning with hands-on problem solving, the Manufacturing Engineering Manager leads critical production improvements, resolves complex manufacturing challenges, and deploys engineering resources to support scalable, high-quality production.
 What you’ll be doing 
 Lead and develop the Manufacturing Engineering and Automation team, providing technical direction, coaching, and project prioritization.
 Own the manufacturing engineering strategy to meet production throughput, standard build times, process capability, and manufacturing efficiency requirements.
 Oversee production line design, workflow, equipment layout, and automation initiatives to support current production and future growth.
 Serve as the technical leader for manufacturing problem solving, providing hands-on leadership to resolve critical line stoppages, product issues, and complex production challenges.
 Drive continuous improvement initiatives through root cause analysis, value stream mapping, Ishikawa (fishbone), and other Lean manufacturing methodologies.
 Own manufacturing tooling strategy and capital equipment planning, including evaluation, implementation, and continuous optimization.
 Prioritize Manufacturing Engineering resources, determining where to personally lead technical initiatives and where to delegate projects across the team to maximize impact.
 Partner with Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, and Product Engineering to support new product introductions and continuously improve manufacturing performance.
 Requirements 
 Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.
 5+ years of manufacturing engineering experience in a complex manufacturing environment (automotive, transportation, heavy equipment, or similar).
 2+ years of leadership experience.
 Full-time site-based role
 Experience with manufacturing process design, automation, tooling, and continuous improvement.
 Strong problem-solving skills with a hands-on approach to supporting production.
 Experience leading projects and working in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
 What we offer 
 A competitive salary and benefits package including group insurance as of day one and RRSP with employer matching
 The opportunity to play a foundational role in shaping the future of outdoor exploration for a leading electric vehicle brand.
 Hands-on experience with Taiga vehicles – experience the impact of your work out in the wild.
 Taiga values diversity in hiring and in its workforce, and welcomes applications from people with diverse backgrounds, education, and experience. We recognize that there are many barriers to equal access to employment and career development opportunities, and we strive to hire groups that are under-represented in the technology industry. Diversity at Taiga means fostering a workplace where differences are valued for the contributions they make to our great team. 
 Thank you for your interest in Taiga. However, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. 
 About Taiga 
 Taiga is a Canadian company reinventing powersports with high-performance electric vehicles built for extraordinary environments. Built on a clean-sheet platform, our vehicles deliver industry-leading power-to-weight performance, advanced thermal systems, and connected technology. From premier ski resorts to pristine waterways, our electric snowmobiles and personal watercraft enable outdoor adventure without compromising the places they operate in.
 For more information about Taiga, visit www.taigamotors.com

Gérer les activités quotidiennes des chantiers.
Comprendre les aspects techniques des mesures de performance énergétique à implanter, afin d’assurer le bon déroulement de l’implantation, la mise en fonction et l’opération de celles-ci. Des défis techniques, nous en avons !
Remettre en question les pratiques établies et proposer des approches innovantes pour atteindre les objectifs, en optimisant budgets, échéanciers et ressources, tout en assurant la performance technique et la coordination de l’équipe.

Baccalauréat en génie mécanique et environ 3 années d’expérience pertinente.
Permis de conduire valide et intérêt pour un rôle orienté terrain, avec une présence quotidienne sur les chantiers.

Vous privilégiez des solutions innovantes plutôt que des approches conventionnelles.

Horaire de chantier atypique, avec une moyenne de 40 heures par semaine.

Opportunités de mentorat et accès illimité à des formations professionnelles.

 Job Description

 Chez GE Vernova, nous relevons chaque jour un défi ambitieux : contribuer à la production d’une énergie plus durable pour les générations futures.
 La lutte contre le changement climatique est une priorité mondiale. En tant qu’entreprise dont la technologie est utilisée pour alimenter environ 25 % de l’électricité dans le monde, nous prenons notre responsabilité au sérieux. GE Vernova est une entreprise qui prend part à une nouvelle ère énergétique – électrifiant le monde tout en travaillant à le décarboniser. Nous accélérons la transition vers une énergie plus fiable, abordable et durable, tout en aidant nos clients à alimenter des économies et à fournir l'électricité essentielle à la santé, à la sûreté, à la sécurité et à l'amélioration de la qualité de vie.
 L'activité Hydroélectrique de GE Vernova conçoit, développe, fabrique et entretient des technologies avancées qui exploitent la puissance de l'eau pour fournir une énergie fiable et durable. Depuis plus d’un siècle, l’hydroélectricité joue un rôle essentiel dans les systèmes électriques nord-américains et mondiaux. Aujourd’hui, il s’agit de la plus grande source d’énergie renouvelable au monde, et la technologie pompage-turbinage représenta la plus grande source de stockage d’énergie. Mais pour atteindre zéro émission nette à l’échelle mondiale d’ici 2050, nous devons doubler la quantité d’hydroélectricité existante. Que ce soit par pompage-turbinage, au fil de l’eau ou en mettant à niveau la base installée existante, l’hydroélectricité continuera d’être la pierre angulaire de l’avenir énergétique de l’Amérique du Nord.

Wealthsimple currently serves more than 4 million Canadians and holds over $155 billion in assets under administration. The company was founded in 2014 by a team of financial experts and technology entrepreneurs, and is headquartered in Toronto, Canada.



We're proud of what we've built — and we're just getting started. Read our Culture Manual https://www.wealthsimple.com/en-ca/culture and learn more about how we work https://www.wealthsimple.com/en-ca/careers.



About the team:

At Wealthsimple, we aren't just managing portfolios; we're rewriting the rules of how Canadians interact with credit. The Credit Analytics team own’s Wealthsimple's lending ecosystem, operating at the intersection of high-growth tech and data-driven underwriting.



We believe that being “credit-worthy” should mean more than just a traditional score. Our mission is to challenge the status quo, building inclusive products that empower millions of Canadians and the businesses they run to lead better financial lives. We’re growing fast, moving from small data to massive scale through iteration and experimentation.



We are extending our consumer credit expertise into business lending built for Canadian small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs). This is a true green-field build — new adjudication policy, new underwriting signals, and new risk infrastructure, informed by everything we've learned scaling our consumer card portfolio.



About the role:

We are looking for a Senior Associate to own credit policy for our business lending products, starting with a business credit card — from adjudication through the full account lifecycle. You will design and implement the underwriting framework that determines who qualifies and at what limit, build the line management strategies that govern how those limits evolve, and partner closely with collections to manage risk once accounts are on book.



Small business cards can be underwritten on the owner, or on the business as it grows. You’ll be working with cash flow, seasonality, industry, and business bureau data, which is usually thinner and messier than consumer bureau data. We need someone who has worked across that range and can turn it into automated policy instead of file-by-file decisions.



You will collaborate cross-functionally with Engineering, Product, Data Science, Fraud, and Client Experience to translate policy into shippable adjudication and monitoring systems, and you will have significant ownership over how this portfolio’s risk appetite is defined from day one.



In this role, you will have the opportunity to:

 - Build a new lending program from the ground up with the breadth to see every part of it, from policy to funding, and the runway to grow into leading a lending line of business.

 - Design and own the adjudication policy for a new business credit card, including entity-level underwriting criteria, principal/guarantor assessment, joint-liability, initial limit-setting, and approval decisioning.

 - Own line management strategy for business credit products: credit limit increases and decreases, pricing, authorization rules, and active exposure management driven by cash-flow and balance monitoring.

 - Partner with the collections team to design risk-managed treatment strategies specific to business accounts, and to build lifecycle monitoring that catches emerging risk early.

 - Evaluate the performance of the business lending portfolio and your policies, using vintage analysis, cohort tracking, and champion/challenger testing to validate and refine underwriting decisions.

 - Propose policy enhancements that improve marginal profitability while keeping risk within appetite, informed by rigorous root-cause analysis rather than surface-level metrics.

 - Help define the data and underwriting infrastructure needed for SMB lending — including how to source, validate, and weigh business financial data alongside traditional bureau signals.

 - Influence roadmaps across partner teams (Engineering, Product, Data Science, Fraud, and Client Experience) and implement policy that drives measurable impact.

We're looking for someone who:

 - Has direct experience underwriting or setting credit policy for small and medium-sized businesses, this is a must-have for this role. Card experience isn't required; we'd love to hear from you if your background is in instalment loans or lines of credit.

 - Writes SQL hands-on to self-serve data and build monitoring and analytics.

 - Brings credit discipline to a ship-and-iterate environment, and is comfortable shaping policy while the product itself is still being defined.

 - Can turn analysis into a clear recommendation for technical and non-technical audiences, weigh incomplete or noisy information and still reach well-grounded decisions.

 - Is intellectually curious, passionate about their work, and wants ownership over their projects.

Preferred qualifications:

 - 5+ years of experience in small business lending

 - Knowledge of Canadian consumer credit bureau data (Equifax, TransUnion)

 - Working knowledge of how business credit risk differs from consumer credit risk: entity vs. personal guarantor assessment, business bureau data (e.g., business credit bureaus), cash-flow-based underwriting, industry/sector risk, and revenue seasonality.

 - Experience across the credit lifecycle: adjudication policy, line management, pricing, and collections strategy.

 - Experience with statistical/quantitative analysis: experimental design, champion/challenger (or A/B) testing, model accuracy validation, constrained optimization, decision trees, discounted cash flows, financial modeling.

 - Experience with Python, and GitHub. Airflow, AWS Redshift, and dbt are a plus.

About Owner

Owner is the AI-native system local business owners use to succeed, starting with restaurants.

We’re building the system that replaces the many tools owners use to run their business.

It powers everything from the restaurant’s website, online ordering, CRM, POS, and more.



Product philosophy

Most small business software makes owners do the work to get what they want: sales growth and profit growth. Owner does the work for them agentically.

Our system drives demand, converts it, and helps operators run their business day to day. As it improves, the business improves with it.

Using Owner should feel like having a team of great operators, engineers, and marketers working for you.



Our vision



We’re starting by helping independent restaurants succeed online.



But it’s not just restaurants that need our help. Most local businesses are struggling with these same problems. Huge technology corporations are taking their customers, bleeding their profits, and making it hard for them to survive.



Once we nail the solution for restaurants – we’ll scale it into every other local business type.



In the future we envision, tens of millions of local business owners will use our technology to succeed in the digital age.



Our traction



Since 2020, we've generated tens of millions in revenue and processed over a billion dollars of online orders. 1 in 5 Americans have used an Owner.com http://Owner.com website.



More importantly, we’ve helped over 20,000 restaurant owners, and saved them nearly $200 million in fees.



Our team



Our team is now in the low hundreds. We’ve got top talent from the most successful companies in SMB software, including: Shopify, HubSpot, DoorDash, ServiceTitan, Rappi, Faire and Stripe.



We’ll be scaling even faster in 2026 to keep pace with our customer growth.



Where we work



Owner is a remote-first, global company headquartered in San Francisco, with a sales hub in Toronto. For a few of our roles we prioritize in-person collaboration at one of our office locations. Most of our teammates are distributed throughout the globe. Please review the role description and discuss with your recruiter for more details on location!





Role Overview

Owner's promise to a restaurant isn't software, it's revenue. When a guest lands on a restaurant's site, we want them to find what they're craving, trust what they see, and check out without friction, whether or not the owner ever touches a setting.

As we scale, we're expanding our product engineering leadership to ship faster, raise the bar on the guest ordering experience, and build the systems that make it work across thousands of restaurants. As the Engineering Manager for OLO, you'll lead a team of full-stack engineers building the guest web ordering experience, from menu, cart and checkout to promotions, photos, and the menu quality systems that make about 10,000 merchant-written menus convert like they were designed by a pro. Next, we're taking OLO to enterprise and multi-location brands, and pushing guest conversion toward 10% through disciplined experimentation. This role is equal parts product intuition and technical execution. You'll be trusted to make hard prioritization calls, ship experiments that move revenue, and grow a team that embodies engineering excellence.

We move with urgency, bias toward simplicity, and expect our leaders to be hands-on when needed. If you're energized by ownership, measurable impact, and solving real problems for small business owners, we'd love to hear from you.

Why we’re looking for you

Owner's promise to a restaurant isn't software — it's revenue. OLO is where that promise gets converted: the guest web ordering experience (menu, cart, checkout, promotions) plus the automated systems that find and fix menu quality problems across roughly 10,000 menus written by merchants we don't control.

We treat conversion as an automated system, not a design review. We build rubrics, detection, and remediation, then prove every change with an experiment. Next, we're taking OLO upmarket to enterprise and multi-location brands and pushing conversion toward 10%.

We're looking for a Senior Engineering Manager to lead the team through that, keep it healthy, and hold a high bar on what we ship and what we cut.

This role is 100% remote and can be based anywhere in the United States or Canada.

Our Stack

 - Web / Growth: React, Next.js, TypeScript — guest web ordering, menu quality, experimentation platform

 - Backend & Services: Node.js, MongoDB → PostgreSQL (migration in flight), Temporal, Datadog

 - Language: TypeScript everywhere

The Impact You'll Have

 - Build the experimentation engine that pushes guest conversion toward 10%, across checkout, fulfillment, merchandising, and promotions

 - Take OLO to enterprise and multi-location brands, with the reliability and menu complexity they need

 - Get >90% of menus, including POS-integrated ones, to our menu quality bar, and build the system that keeps live menus optimized as they change

 - Scale photo coverage using guest sourcing, auto-replating, licensed catalogs, and generated combo images, each tied to measured GPV lift

 - Rebuild promotions from the ground up: redemption UX, badges, auto-apply, and merchandising

 - Cut fulfillment selection errors and finish the Postgres migration

What we’re looking for

 - 3+ years of engineering management, leading teams of 6–10+ engineers on customer-facing product

 - Track record of running growth or conversion programs: metrics, A/B testing at scale, funnel analysis

 - Experience scaling a product for enterprise or multi-location customers

 - Strong prioritization: you can take a roadmap bigger than your team and make hard, clear calls

 - Technical credibility in full-stack web (React/TypeScript, Node.js) and data-heavy systems

 - Cares about team health and has led people through heavy or repetitive workloads

 - Excellent cross-functional partner to PM, design, and adjacent teams

Compensation and benefits

 - The estimated base salary range for this role is $250K-$270K, depending on experience and location. The offer also includes a a generous pre-IPO equity package.

 - Other benefits include comprehensive health coverage, remote-first workplace, unlimited PTO - plus extra fun perks!





Notice - Employment Scams

Communication from our team regarding job opportunities will only be made by an Owner team member with an @owner.com email address.



We do not conduct interviews over email or chat platforms, and we will never ask you to provide personal or financial information such as your mailing address, social security number, credit card numbers or banking information. If you believe you are being contacted by a scammer, please mark the communication as "phishing" or “spam” and do not respond.

Client Success Specialist 
 Town Web · HeyGov · ClerkMinutes. Remote, Central US hours.
 About us 
 We make municipal software built for clerks: websites residents can use, forms and payments that replace stacks of paper, and meeting minutes drafted after every meeting. More than 1,300 local governments rely on us, from counties and cities to villages and towns. We have local government customers in almost every state in the U.S.
 Our clients are municipal clerks and the government teams around them. They keep city hall running and rarely get thanked for it. Your job is to make working with us the easy part of their week.
 The role 
 Our AI agent now answers repeatable, well-documented questions. What is left is the work that  only a person can do: own a client's problem from the first message to the confirmed fix, build a relationship a clerk trusts, and turn what you learn into better documentation and a better product.
 This is not a ticket-closing job. Think of a great 5-star hotel that puts slippers by the bed before you ask. We want a clerk to finish a conversation with you and tell the clerk in the next town about the great experience they had. If that takes three calls, take three calls.
 It is also a technical job. You will work with our developers every day. When something breaks, you work out where it lives before anyone else has to. Is the problem occurring on the events calendar on the client’s homepage, or is happening within the calendar of events widget that is embedded on a department page? Is the wrong speaker name showing up only in the transcript or is it showing up in the finished minutes? You reproduce it, write it up so a developer can act without a follow-up question, stay on it until it ships, and tell the client yourself.
 What you will do 
 Delight clients 
 Make every interaction feel personal, warm, and unhurried, especially for less technical users who would rather talk to a person than read a help article
 Step in when the AI agent or the documentation is not enough, and make sure the client feels heard and helped, not processed
 Treat client sentiment as the real measure of success, not ticket speed
 Look for small moments to go above and beyond, and share what works so it becomes how the whole team operates
 Own the problem from start to finish 
 Be the named person on an account when things go wrong: one owner, one plan, regular updates, until the client says it is fixed
 Step in early when an account shows strain (repeat tickets, a rough launch, a frustrated message) and run the recovery. Get on a call, write down what is open, set dates, follow through
 Make sure nothing sits untracked once it leaves the support queue
 Diagnose, then escalate 
 Work out which product and which layer an issue lives in before you hand it to a developer

 We spend real money to reach older adults who need mental health care, and most of them are not on the internet the way your last audience was.  About Total Life
 Total Life is a national behavioral health telehealth platform built for later-life adults. 200+ licensed clinicians, 49+ states, and we bill Original Medicare Part B directly — which means for most of the people we serve, therapy costs them little to nothing. That's an unusually strong offer, and our job is to get it in front of the people who need it.
 We ranked #5 in the healthcare category on the Inc. 5000, with growth over 5,000% since 2021. We are still small enough that this hire will change the trajectory of the company.
 What you'll own
 Full-funnel paid acquisition across Google, Meta, YouTube, Bing, Reddit, Quora, Nextdoor, and native networks — plus whatever you can prove out next.
 Traditional and offline demand generation. Direct mail, print, radio, CTV/linear, community and senior-center partnerships. Our audience is 65+, and a large share of our best prospects will never click an ad. You'll be responsible for building programs that reach them anyway, with attribution good enough to defend the spend.
 ROAS and CAC as your scoreboard. Not impressions, not MQLs. You own blended CAC, channel-level ROAS, and cost per completed intake.
 Creative strategy. You'll direct the concepting, testing, and iteration of ad creative — you don't have to be the designer, but you have to know what to test and why, and you have to be able to tell a creative team something more useful than "make it pop."
 Measurement infrastructure. Attribution across a long, offline-heavy funnel is genuinely hard here. You'll define how we know what's working, including for channels with no click.
 Budget allocation. You'll bring us a monthly plan for where the money goes, defend it with numbers, and change it when the numbers change.
 What we're looking for
 Non-negotiable: 
 You have personally managed $30K+/month in spend on multiple individual channels — not a $30K/month total book split six ways. We want to see depth, at scale, on more than one channel.
 Direct experience on both digital and traditional/offline channels. Real spend, real results, in both worlds.
 A track record you can put numbers to: starting ROAS, ending ROAS, over what period, on what spend, and what you actually changed to get there.
 Fluency in the analytics stack — GA4, ad platform reporting, a CRM (we run HubSpot), and enough comfort in spreadsheets or SQL to check your platforms' math rather than take their word for it.

 Direct response with a phone-based or human-assisted conversion path.
 You've built a channel from zero, not just optimized an inherited one.

 One channel you scaled. The channel, the monthly spend, the ROAS or CAC before and after, the time frame, and the two or three specific decisions that moved it. Numbers or it didn't happen.

 Your first-90-days hypothesis for us. Look at our ads, our site, and our offer. Where would you put the next $50K, and what would you expect to get for it? Two paragraphs is plenty — we're reading for thinking, not polish.
